urbanization-origins-s2.title: A history of an invented river town
urbanization-origins-s2.html:
Invented passage for practice. "Our town began about 900 years ago on a rocky island where the river narrows, so it was easy to defend and to cross. For centuries it grew because the coast road met the river route inland at our bridge, and every merchant paid a toll. In the 1880s the harbor filled with silt, and the new railroad was laid 30 kilometers to the north, through the town of Hartfield. Trade moved there. Our island is as safe and as pretty as ever, but our population has not grown since."

From a local history society booklet (invented), 1952.

cities-globalization-s2.title: How one shipment of phones gets made
cities-globalization-s2.html: Invented passage for practice, 2026. A company headquartered in a world city signs a contract with a factory in Viet Nam to build two million phones. The money is lent by a bank in London. A law firm in New York checks the contract, and both sides sign it by video call in under an hour. An advertising agency in Tokyo plans the launch. A port company in Singapore books the ships. The factory workers in Viet Nam never meet any of these people, but their hours depend on decisions made in those offices.

city-structure-s2.title: Field notes from a city in Latin America
city-structure-s2.html: Invented field notes for practice, 2026. "We started at the cathedral on the main plaza, among banks and government offices. From there a wide avenue lined with office towers, embassies and mansions runs west for eight kilometers to a new shopping mall and a gated suburb. In the other directions, the houses near the center are old but solid. Farther out, families are adding second floors to concrete homes. On the dry hills at the city's edge, people who arrived in the last few years have built houses from brick and metal sheets on land they do not own. Water arrives by truck twice a week."

Invented interviews for practice, 2026.

Rosa, 68, renter for 40 years: "My rent went up three times in four years. Most of my friends from church have moved to the suburbs. I still love this street, but it does not feel like mine."

Marcus, 34, bought a house in 2019: "We picked East Ridge for the old houses and the bus line downtown. The neighbors were kind to us, but I know some people see us as the reason prices went up."

urban-change-challenges-s1.title: A public hearing on a riverfront plan
urban-change-challenges-s1.html:
Invented passage for practice, 2026. At a city council hearing on a city redevelopment plan to clear and replace a closed rail yard and 200 older rental homes with 1,500 new apartments, offices and a riverside park:

A developer: "This plan brings 2,000 jobs, a new park and 10 million dollars a year in taxes."

A renter of 22 years: "My building is on your map. Where will my family go? Nothing in this city is affordable to us."

A city planner: "We propose that 20% of the new apartments be priced for families earning less than the city's median income."

items.q: Which statement best describes the distribution of the hearths marked A, B and C on the map?

items.q: Each hearth marked A, B and C lay in a fairly dry region crossed by a large river (the Nile, the Indus and the Huang He). Which explains why the first cities grew in places like these?

items.q: Town 1 has 200 thousand people and Town 2 has 50 thousand. They are 10 units apart. Using the gravity model <math class="hug-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>×</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{P_1 \times P_2}{d^2}</annotation></semantics></math> with populations in thousands, what is the interaction score?

mistakes.why: You divided by the distance, not by its square. Square it first: <math class="hug-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^2 = 100</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math class="hug-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>10000</mn><mn>100</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{10000}{100}</annotation></semantics></math>.

You left out the distance. Divide by the distance squared: <math class="hug-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>10000</mn><mn>100</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{10000}{100}</annotation></semantics></math>.
